quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Studies show that nearly ______ of motorcycle riders killed in crashes had been drinking.

options.text: 20 percent
40 percent
60 percent
80 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 40 percent
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a major cause of motorcycle crashes and deaths. Studies show that about 40 percent of riders killed in motorcycle crashes had been drinking.

questions.question: If a small animal enters your lane while you are riding in traffic, you should:

options.text: Swerve into other lanes to avoid hitting the animal.
Change lanes as quickly as possible.
Stay in your lane.
Flash your lights to scare the animal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in your lane when riding in traffic, even if a small animal is in your way. Swerving into another lane could cause you to hit another vehicle. Hitting a small animal is safer than hitting another car.

questions.question: A linked braking system:

options.text: Connects the front and rear brakes so both brakes work when either brake lever is used.
Connects the front brake to the gear shifter and applies the brake when downshifting.
Connects the rear brake to a foot control.
Connects the rear brake to a handlebar switch.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connects the front and rear brakes so both brakes work when either brake lever is used.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes. When you use either the front or rear brake lever, both brakes receive pressure. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: Because of their small size, motorcycles may appear to be:

options.text: Moving faster than they really are.
Moving slower than they really are.
Stopped when they are actually moving.
Closer than they really are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Moving faster than they really are.
questions.explanation: Because motorcycles are small, they may look like they are going faster than they actually are.

questions.question: When riding in a group, less experienced riders should position themselves:

options.text: Just behind the leader.
In front of the group.
At the back of the group.
Next to the leader.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front of the group, just behind the leader. This lets more experienced riders watch them and help if needed.

questions.question: The front brake supplies about how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?

options.text: About 25 percent
About 50 percent
About 70 percent
100 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake and provides about 70 percent of your motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Slow or stop
Left turn
Right turn
Backing up

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow or stop
questions.explanation: You can use hand signals instead of or along with brake lights to tell other drivers what you plan to do. If you bend your left arm at the elbow and point downward, it means you are slowing down or stopping.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, you should NOT:

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Avoid making sudden moves.
Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
Use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes, slow down, and avoid sudden moves. Watch out for oil, dirt, gravel, shade, and bridges, as these areas are more slippery.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both actions at the same time.
Always brake first, then swerve.
Use only the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: If you need to brake and swerve, do them one at a time. You can brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake. Do not do both at the same time.

questions.question: Which vest or jacket color helps you be seen the most?

options.text: Red
Black
Silver
Blue

questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors while riding to be more visible. Bright orange, yellow, red, or green works best. Avoid dark or dull colors.

questions.question: In hot weather, wearing a riding jacket:

options.text: Can help protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
Is discouraged because it can cause heat-related problems.
Should only be done if the jacket is a light color.
Is not important.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: You should wear a riding jacket and long pants in hot weather. They protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration, in addition to other safety benefits.

questions.question: Should you wear a leather jacket while riding in warm weather?

options.text: No, it will make you too hot.
Yes, but take frequent breaks to remove the jacket and cool off.
Yes, riding jackets are made to keep the rider cool, even in warm weather.
No, jackets get in the way of steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, riding jackets are made to keep the rider cool, even in warm weather.
questions.explanation: In warm weather, a riding jacket helps prevent dehydration and provides protection. Many jackets are designed to protect riders from overheating, even when it is warm.

questions.question: When traveling in a group, riders should:

options.text: Spread out to make the group easier to see.
Stay close together to make the group easier to see.
Separate occasionally.
Ride in pairs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay close together to make the group easier to see.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, stay close together while leaving enough space around each rider to maneuver. This makes the group easier to see and prevents riders from becoming separated. Do not pair up because it does not leave enough room to maneuver.

questions.question: A motorcyclist can discourage other vehicles from lane sharing by:

options.text: Riding in the left portion of a lane.
Riding in the center portion of a lane.
Giving dirty looks if another driver moves into their lane.
Riding in a zigzag pattern to fill up a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in the center portion of a lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center portion of your lane to discourage other drivers from trying to squeeze into the space next to you.

questions.question: A helmeted rider is _______ more likely to survive a crash than a rider not wearing a helmet.

options.text: Two times
Three times
Six times
20 times

questions.correctAnswerText: Three times
questions.explanation: Riders who wear helmets are three times more likely to survive a crash than riders who do not wear helmets. This is true at any speed.

questions.question: When an operator's left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward, it means the operator:

options.text: Plans to turn left.
Is about to stop.
Plans to turn right.
Is about to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plans to turn right.
questions.explanation: Operators can use hand signals instead of mechanical turn signals. When the left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward, it means the operator plans to turn right or change lanes to the right.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle and trying to turn, you should:

options.text: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the grip opposite of the direction you want to turn.
Not hold the grip because it can be dangerous.
Not lean the motorcycle as that can be unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: When traveling faster than a walking pace, your motorcycle must lean to turn. Press the grip in the direction you want to turn to lean the motorcycle in the right direction.

questions.question: When planning a long group ride, which of the following ideas should not be implemented?

options.text: The lengths of travel segments should be based on the least experienced rider.
Breaks should be minimized so the riders can get to their destination as soon as possible.
Inexperienced riders should be placed behind the leaders.
The group should maintain a staggered riding formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Breaks should be minimized so the riders can get to their destination as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Plan ride segments based on the least experienced rider's skill level. Take regular breaks to reduce fatigue. Place inexperienced riders behind the leader so experienced riders can watch them. Ride in a staggered formation.

questions.question: Maximum straight-line braking is done by:

options.text: Using the front brake, then the rear brake.
Using the rear brake, then the front brake.
Using the front and rear brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
Using the front and rear brakes at the same time while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using the front and rear brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: Maximum straight-line braking happens when you apply both the front and rear brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.

questions.question: A passenger on a motorcycle should:

options.text: Mount the motorcycle before the engine starts.
Mount the motorcycle after the engine starts.
Sit as close to the rear of the motorcycle as possible.
Hold onto the seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Mount the motorcycle after the engine starts.
questions.explanation: Passengers should get on the motorcycle only after the engine starts and the transmission is in neutral. They should sit as far forward as possible without blocking the operator's control and should hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What should you use when riding in rain or fog?

options.text: High beam headlight.
Low beam headlight.
No headlight.
Switch between low and high beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlight.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, or fog. High beams reflect off these conditions and make it harder to see.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular in shape?

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black lettering. These regulatory signs tell drivers what rules to follow on the road.

questions.question: How should you brake?

options.text: Front brake first, then rear brake.
Rear brake first, then front brake.
Both brakes at the same time.
Brakes in any order.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Which is NOT important when choosing a helmet?

options.text: It meets DOT safety standards.
It looks nice.
It fits snugly.
It has no defects.

questions.correctAnswerText: It looks nice.
questions.explanation: A good helmet must meet DOT safety standards, fit snugly around your head, and have no damage like cracks or loose straps. How it looks is not important for safety.

questions.question: Why should you not ride too far to the right with a three-wheeled motorcycle or sidecar?

options.text: Other drivers may not see you.
You will not pass other vehicles as easily.
Other drivers may try to share your lane.
You may run off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may run off the road.
questions.explanation: A sidecar sits on the right side of the motorcycle. The rear right wheel of a three-wheeled motorcycle can also leave the road. Riding too far right puts these parts off the edge.
